messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager: network-slo-high latency increase in az1a affecting inference requests (p95 RTT spikes to 800ms, error rate +6%). Paging oncall-1 and netops. Please ack and triage

oncall-1: acked. seeing alerts on latency dashboard and healthcheck flaps for /v1/generate across several instances in az1a. Diving in now.

sasha.nguyen: I can see repeated ENIC resets on instance i-0abc1234 in az1a from cloudwatch: NetworkInterfaceDetach/Attach events every ~30s. Kernel logs show NIC flaps and tcp retransmits.

netops: thx Sasha. Any sign of host-level saturation or host link errors? packet drops?

sasha.nguyen: host rx_queue backlog climbs then kernel logs with "NETDEV WATCHDOG" and "device eth0 entered promiscuous mode" (weird). Also dmesg: "enic0: reset recovery". Suspect NIC firmware or hypervisor-side soft reset.

maria_g: customers noticing 502s and high tail latency. Support already triaged 4 high-impact accounts flagged by SLO monitors. We should open interim customer comms.

oncall-1: immediate mitigation idea: start steering 30% of az1a traffic to az1b/az1c for inference routes, and increase retries with region failover policy. Can ops/infra apply weight change on the routing tier?

netops: copying commands. We can update LB weights. Suggested quick command: 
```
# set az1a weight 70, az1b weight 15, az1c weight 15
redwood-route update --pool inference-prod --region az1a=70,az1b=15,az1c=15
```

tj: also recommend enabling model-variant fallback to a smaller quantized variant in other AZs to keep latency low while capacity is reduced. I can push the rollout policy in 2 mins.

engr-runner: starting a canary reroute now (targeting 25% cross-az traffic). Monitoring token-per-second and error-rate.

incident-bot: Action required: oncall-1 assigned -> network investigation. Severity: SEV2.

oncall-1: netops, please drain the worst hosts in az1a after steering in case of persistent ENI resets. Steps: cordon and drain k8s nodes with affected instances, then trigger an instance replacement. Use graceful drain window 60s.

netops: acknowledged. Running: `kubectl cordon node/gpu-az1a-12 && kubectl drain node/gpu-az1a-12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=60`

sasha.nguyen: logs from instance show repeated TCP RESET and kernel backtrace referencing enic driver. I'm attaching the snippet: 
```
Mar 3 12:41:02 kernel: enic 0000:00:1f.6 eth0: ENIC reset attempt 1
Mar 3 12:41:32 kernel: enic 0000:00:1f.6 eth0: ENIC reset attempt 2
Mar 3 12:42:02 kernel: eth0: rx err -89, dropped 200 packets
```

maria_g: Support: Flagged 9 customer sessions degraded; two enterprise customers reported timed requests and retry storms. Need status update for status.redwood.ai within 15m.

oncall-1: Drafting status: "We are seeing increased errors and latency for inference requests in a single AZ (az1a). Traffic is being partially rerouted while we replace affected hosts. Some requests may see increased latency or transient errors. No data loss. Engineering investigating." Anyone add to that?

tj: add that we enabled cross-AZ fallback and are performing node replacements; advising customers to enable retry with region fallback if they control clients.

netops: drain of 3 bad nodes completed. Started instance replacement via autoscaling group: `aws autoscaling terminate-instance-in-auto-scaling-group --instance-id i-0abc1234 --no-should-decrement-desired-capacity`

incident-bot: Note: automated evictions observed for pods on gpu-az1a-12 due to network stall; eviction rate 0.7/min.

engr-runner: After reroute to 30% cross-az, p95 dropped from 800ms -> 320ms. Error rate down from +6% -> +1.2%. Looks promising.

sasha.nguyen: however, new instances from ASG show same driver version. If this is a host-level hypervisor issue, replacement may not help. Netops, can we move traffic away from the problematic placement group or use different instance type temporarily?

netops: we can spin up replacement nodes in az1b under same ASG by setting desired capacity in az1b and decreasing az1a, but that's a bit manual. Quick option: use cross-zone pool failover while we coordinate with AWS support. I'll raise an AWS ticket with EC2 team: "ENI resets and RX queue saturation in az1a affecting multiple instances" and request CC.

maria_g: Support: we posted initial notice on status.customers asked for impact window — we don't know yet. Please keep comms updated every 15 minutes.

oncall-1: escalation: if we can't reach stable in 30m, escalate to SEV1 and engage account execs for the affected customers.

tj: quick runbook note for others: if you see ENIC resets + dropped packets + high rx queue, try temporary mitigations: 1) traffic steer 2) drain nodes 3) increase retry/backoff 4) enable model fallback 5) engage AWS.

netops: AWS case opened: 1234567890. AWS response ETA 45m. They requested tcp dump and degraded host IDs — uploaded.

sasha.nguyen: collecting tcpdump: `tcpdump -i eth0 -w /tmp/az1a-enic-flap.pcap` and uploading to the case. Also capturing `ethtool -S eth0` counters.

incident-bot: Reminder: oncall handover scheduled in 1h. If still active, please coordinate shift change.

engr-runner: Observability note: KV cache hit rate dipped for inference models served from az1a by ~12% during the flaps (clients reconnected). That's contributing to tail latency.

maria_g: Support to customers: one partner asked for a temporary quota increase to redirect workloads to other regions; ops, can you allow immediate cross-region bursting for partner-123?

netops: we can allow cross-region bursts by creating a temporary policy. Applying now.

oncall-1: current status update: traffic steered (~30% cross-az), drained 5 nodes, ASG replacements in progress, AWS case open. Observed latency improvement, but still higher-than-normal tail. Keeping SEV2. Next check in 15m.

incident-bot: Update logged. Timeline event: 00:12 mitigation - traffic steer applied; 00:24 node drain started; 00:40 AWS case opened.

sasha.nguyen: follow-up: If AWS confirms host NIC hardware issue, we may need to mark affected placement and migrate workloads. Plan to run extended canary for 1h then consider full failover of az1a for inference pool if unstable.

maria_g: adding post-incident actions: 1) ensure better detection rule for ENI reset patterns; 2) validate autoscaling replacement variants across AZs; 3) tabletop with AWS account team.

netops: AWS replied: preliminary feedback points to hypervisor NIC reset affecting EC2 Nitro network stack in a subset of hosts in az1a. They are performing capacity move and host replacement. ETA for remediation: 2-3 hours.

oncall-1: given ETA, keep SEV2 and prepare for extended mitigation: increase cross-az steer to 50% if error-rate creeps back. Also prepare support template for longer outage.

tj: I'll schedule a rollback to purely hosted model-variant fallback in case we need to reduce cross-AZ data egress.

engr-runner: monitoring looks stable with current settings; error rate steady ~1.1% and p95 ~310ms. Keeping watch.

maria_g: updating customer comms: noted AWS ETA ~2-3h. Customers asking for RCA once resolved. We'll mark action items for postmortem.

incident-bot: oncall handoff reminder: shift change in 40m. If anyone wants to take the remaining watch, react with :raised_hand:.

sasha.nguyen: +1 to handoff if still ongoing. I'll take first watch and follow up on AWS case.

oncall-1: handing off to sasha.nguyen for next 2h. I'll stay reachable for escalation. Closing immediate actions for me.

sasha.nguyen: ack. continuing to monitor and pushing updated pcap and logs to AWS case. Will update thread every 20m or on material changes.

incident-bot: Thread archived by oncall actions. Please update postmortem once resolved."
